subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `messages.operationalReplies` and fail-closed operator-session redirect as a public core delivery contract?
rationale: Mechanical changes can repair reservation cleanup and storage, but cannot decide whether the new configuration, plugin signal, durable semantics, and intentional source suppression should become supported product behavior.

options.title: Approve after repairs
options.body: Confirm the direction, require exception-safe delivery and canonical SQLite storage, then merge only after exact-head proof is clean.

options.title: Reduce the public surface
options.body: Retain only a narrower approved suppression mode and remove redirect or durable `once` semantics.

options.title: Decline the feature
options.body: Close the PR if core should not own a global operational-notice contract.

recommendation.title: Approve after repairs
recommendation.body: Confirm the direction, require exception-safe delivery and canonical SQLite storage, then merge only after exact-head proof is clean.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across the affected delivery, configuration, persistence, and plugin-contract surfaces.
